extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing responses to peer review (early-career and experienced researchers submitting manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for authors on how to read, prioritize, document, and respond to peer reviewers' comments when revising a manuscript, including handling ambiguous or ethical situations and using tools (e.g., AI) appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize responses using tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tables to organize responses to reviewers so each comment and the corresponding author action is clearly recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suggestion to use tables is described as excellent and often recommended: tables allow a clear, organized presentation of how each comment was addressed, helping reviewers and editors easily follow changes. No specific table format is mandated, but entries should map reviewer comment → author response → manuscript location of change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize feedback (major vs minor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize reviewer comments into major and minor critiques and focus first on major revisions that directly impact methodology, results, or conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice: prioritize items that influence the study’s core (e.g., clarifications of data analysis, requests for additional experiments) before minor grammatical or stylistic corrections. The text gives examples: major comments include modifying the central hypothesis, the main algorithm, or redoing an experiment; minor remarks include unclear statements, missing/incorrect references, unclear data presentation, grammatical concerns, adding a paragraph/table/figure, or adding an appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professionalism and constructive tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Be polite and respectful in responses; do not personalize critiques and express gratitude appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are advised to remain objective, avoid responding to tone (e.g., do not call out harsh wording), and focus on content. Use a concise, well-crafted expression of thanks (avoid repetitive gratitude). Example opening: “We thank the reviewer for their insightful feedback on our methodology.” Keep language courteous throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek guidance from editors or mentors when unsure
rubrics_metrics.description: If uncertain how to address a particular comment, consult the journal editor (e.g., editor-in-chief) or a knowledgeable mentor for advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, authors are encouraged to reach out to the editor or a mentor with subject-matter expertise to clarify whether and how to implement a requested change. This helps ensure responses are appropriate and aligned with journal expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow journal guidelines and seek editorial approval for conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers' requests conflict with the journal's policies or with the authors' legitimate choices, consult the editor and follow the journal guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance respecting reviewers' suggestions and preserving the authors’ original vision. If a reviewer asks for actions that contradict journal policy or are outside scope, seek editorial approval rather than unilaterally making changes. Streamline references to relevant policies where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document changes clearly in the response letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear, organized response letter that methodically addresses each reviewer point and documents the exact changes made in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break down complex reviewer comments into manageable parts and address each point methodically. For each comment, state whether you made a change or explain why no change was made, and indicate where in the manuscript the change appears (e.g., section, page, paragraph, line). This documentation aids reviewers and editors in verifying revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI tools cautiously and as a supplementary aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat AI proofreading/assistive tools as supplementary measures; do not rely on them as the primary method of revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI tools may not catch all linguistic nuances or contextual errors; authors are advised to use them to support, not replace, careful human review. The manuscript added explicit wording warning that AI can lead to oversight and that authors should ensure a balanced and thorough proofreading process (and refer readers to appendices for more detail if provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to established ethical guidelines for ambiguous situations
rubrics_metrics.description: For ambiguous or ethical issues (e.g., suspected undeclared conflicts of interest, concerns about reviewer behavior or AI-assisted reviews), consult recognized bodies such as COPE and ICMJE and alert editors when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE), International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE), or similar guidance for handling conflicts of interest and other ethical issues. If an author suspects a reviewer used AI-assisted technologies without disclosure, they should notify the editor. Following these guidelines helps maintain the integrity of the peer review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify and exemplify major vs minor reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concrete examples to distinguish major and minor reviewer comments so authors can apply the prioritization strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: Major — modify central hypothesis, change main algorithm, redo an experiment; Minor — unclear wording, missing/incorrect references, data presentation tweaks, grammar, adding small figures/tables or appendices. Including such examples helps authors judge how to prioritize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid copying reviewers' comments verbatim into the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not copy-paste reviewers' phrasing into the manuscript; instead paraphrase and integrate suggestions in your own words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarizing reviewers' comments (e.g., copying a reviewer’s text verbatim into the paper) is flagged as problematic. If a reviewer’s suggestion improves the manuscript, rephrase and incorporate the idea in the authors’ own voice rather than reproducing the reviewer’s wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge reviewers in acknowledgements when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider formally acknowledging reviewers whose feedback substantially improved the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice (suggested by a reviewer) demonstrates appreciation beyond the response letter and can foster goodwill. Only do so when the reviewer’s contributions materially improved the work and when journal policy permits or recommends such acknowledgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise thoroughly with attention to documentation, communication, and final review
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the revision process includes careful documentation of edits, clear communication among co-authors, and a final review for quality and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section emphasizes professionalism and attention to detail: keep records of changes, coordinate responses among co-authors, perform a final read-through to eliminate redundancies (e.g., repeated gratitude) and ensure clarity before resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle reviewer requests to omit citations of specific authors by consulting the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer asks that specific authors not be cited (e.g., due to reputational concerns), determine whether the request targets the individual or the research and consult the editor privately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests may be sensitive; authors should not unilaterally remove citations for reputational reasons. Instead, contact the editor to discuss the best course of action and to ensure ethical handling consistent with journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond substantively: implement changes or defend with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: For substantive critiques, either implement the requested changes or provide a reasoned, evidence-based rebuttal in the response letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing to defend an approach rather than change it, provide clear justification and cite supporting literature or data. Responses should be thoughtful, focused on evidence, and not dismissive.
